ninfer_qwen3_5_dflash_real_test.reason: This route needs a `dflash` component and this product's artifacts ship `dflash2` instead: the shipped artifact's config lists dflash2 (architectures ['DFlash2DraftModel']) and no dflash, so the route cannot pass here by construction. The engine rejects the request precisely -- 'Qwen3.5 config: missing component dflash', reproduced through the shipped CLI with --spec dflash --draft-tokens 3 --vision --max-context 4096 --prefill-chunk 1024, which exits 1 in 0.1 s with that message -- but the test had no try/catch, so the rejection reached std::terminate and the process died with 0xC0000409 (ucrtbase, BEX64) in ~2.1 s printing nothing. The test now catches it and prints the engine's message, so a failure names its cause. Baselined rather than skipped so the gate stays truthful about it, matching moe_real_test.

ninfer_qwen3_5_moe_real_test.reason: Needs a 35B-A3B MoE checkpoint (tests/README.md names qwen3_6_35b_a3b.ninfer). This product ships three artifacts and all are 27B dense, so it cannot pass here by construction, and the fail-fast happens before any model load. Baselined because a rule that demands an artifact outside the product would block every release forever.

ninfer_qwen3_5_moe_offload_real_test.reason: Needs a 35B-A3B MoE checkpoint, as its sibling ninfer_qwen3_5_moe_real_test does. Measured here with a 27B dense artifact (C:\AI\models\qwen3_8_27b_nvfp4nvidia.v3.ninfer): planning rejects it with 'VRAM budget cannot hold this model and its execution resources', which is the message at src/runtime/engine/model_instance.cpp:132 -- the resident plan does not fit, so planning falls through to the MoE branch and throws because the architecture is not Qwen3_5Moe (model_instance.cpp:130). So the refusal is the test refusing the wrong artifact, not a defect: the offload path is unexercised here and the coverage is missing, not satisfied. Baselined for the same reason as the sibling -- this product's artifacts cannot satisfy the test, and a gate that demands an artifact outside the product would block every release forever.

ninfer_linear_swiglu_nvfp4_test.reason: A deliberate divergence, not an impossibility -- unlike the three entries above it. Upstream's consolidated runner hard-codes a rejection at NVFP4 A16 T=17 (tests/ops/linear/swiglu/runner.cpp:431, CallForm::RejectA16Extent) because upstream's NVFP4 A16 family stops at T=16 (src/ops/linear/swiglu/nvfp4/shapes/n34816_k5120/a16.cu: SIMT to 2, sliced-K to 8, sliced-K to 16). This port registers an A16 route at every extent: the MatrixFusedA16 branch in nvfp4/shapes/n34816_k5120/dispatch.cpp, built from the same Nvfp4A16MmaSchedule instances the registered [34816,5120] Linear uses and mirroring upstream's own launch_fp8_swiglu_matrix for the FP8 format. So the case asserts the opposite of what this tree does, and it is NOT deleted from runner.cpp: that file is upstream-owned, so a deletion there is re-conflicted on every merge, while this entry is in a port-owned file. The extent itself is covered by cases_nvfp4.cpp's 19-extent A16 profile, which includes 17 and asserts it against the numerical criterion -- the surviving coverage is the stronger one. What upstream does above T=16 instead is the linear + silu_mul decomposition, measured at 8.1e-3 against the profile's 6.3e-3 tail bound (RELEASE_NOTES.md), which is what this route replaced. Remove this entry if the route is ever withdrawn; the gate fails on a stale baseline entry, which is the ratchet working.

note: Green since 2026-09-19. The former failure, test_candidate_search_prefers_deep_reuse_without_eviction, was caused by the optional materialization search's initial grant being pinned flat at 5 ms; a flat cap dominated whenever the incumbent was expensive, so the search verified too few targets and admission could fall back to one-step eviction or to the root incumbent and re-prefill the prompt (upstream issue #229). The grant now scales with the incumbent's cost up to a 250 ms ceiling, governed by the economic term and the boundary allowance (src/runtime/engine/context_cache/materialization_budget.h). That file, the planner it lived in and the test above were all removed by upstream b9114396, and the port's version of them was not carried into the replacement, so the grant's behaviour under the new context cache has not been re-measured and upstream issue #229 is still open. required_tests lists the real-model tests this product must run and pass; every other real test is named under optional_tests with the reason it cannot be required, because a blanket rule would demand evidence this product cannot produce. Failures in any test, required or not, still fail the gate. Size moved from 124 to 130 on 2026-09-25 with the upstream merge of bace20dc, which registered four sync-mode tests plus the invalid and empty startup cases; the empty case sets its variable through `cmake -E env` rather than ctest's ENVIRONMENT, because decorating a test with ENVIRONMENT "NINFER_CUDA_SYNC=" makes the test pass and poisons every test after it -- 36 failed that way before it was found. Size moved from 130 to 132 on 2026-09-26 with the upstream merge of e31bc99b, but not for the reason the counts alone suggest: that merge added exactly one test, ninfer_kimi_delta_attention_test, by adding one line (`kimi_delta_attention`) to the ninfer_op_tests list in tests/ops/tests.cmake, which was the only file under tests/ it touched and which had no removals -- so the pre-merge suite was 131, and the recorded 130 was already one low before this merge. Counting the additions from the diff alone would have credited the merge with two; the count is derived from the verified single-line diff against the verified current total, not from comparing recorded numbers. Size moved from 132 to 135 on 2026-09-27 with the ported ngram tests, and the total did not move again when the copy-drafting design was replaced the same day. The first three were ninfer_ngram_proposer_test, ninfer_ngram_graph_planning_test and ninfer_ngram_archive_test; the proposer and archive were then withdrawn with the design that needed them and replaced by ninfer_ngram_pool_test and ninfer_ngram_policy_test, so the suite is 135 - 2 + 2 and the graph-planning test is the only one of the four that survived unchanged. All are host-only and need no artifact, so required_tests and optional_tests are unchanged throughout. They are in the gate now rather than with the wiring because the copy-drafting core is worth proving correct before anything routes a token through it. Two of them carry a weight beyond coverage: the pool test pins the same hash vector as the source fork's offline simulator, which is what makes that simulator a valid predictor of this pool's slots, tags and collisions; and the graph-planning test pins the masked-draft planner's refusal of a width above the round's 15-column domain. Size moved from 135 to 136 on 2026-09-27 with ninfer_ngram_selection_test, the masked-draft copy-selection decision: header-only, host-only, and swept over 1,080 input combinations at its boundary, because both of its failure modes are silent in production -- widening a round the copy cannot pay for, and dropping a copy that would have paid. ninfer_ngram_policy_test was withdrawn on 2026-09-28 along with the chain policy it tested -- ngram_policy.h had no production caller once the selection design replaced it, and existed only to keep that test alive. That takes the suite from 136 to 135. The selection test itself lost a dimension with the withdrawn wide round: it no longer sweeps a verify window, so its boundary cases fall from 1,080 to 340. The graph-planning and selection tests both remain, host-only, so required_tests and optional_tests are unchanged. The pool test went with the pool on 2026-09-28: ninfer_ngram_pool_test is replaced by ninfer_prompt_lookup_test, so the suite holds at 135. PromptLookup is ported from satellitedown/cinference (HEAD 1d07410, Apache-2.0, which lists it among its own added paths rather than inheriting it from NInfer) and is a strictly better proposer than the pool: it matches three window lengths instead of one configured length, re-checks the matched tokens so a hash collision cannot become a wrong proposal, and carries a learned decayed per-window acceptance estimate, which is the signal ngram_selection.h had recorded as an open question and had to gate on a bare length threshold without. It is per-sequence and allocates lazily, so the shared pool it replaces took with it the startup sizing, the ngram_pool-has-a-value invariant, and the --ngram-n and --ngram-pool-mib options, whose fields nothing read any more. Its test is host-only and needs no library beyond the model runtime. Like the pool before it, PromptLookup has no consumer yet: the verify tree that is meant to consume it -- candidate_selector_tree, tree_parents, tree-aware GDN replay and target attention, a tree accept Op -- does not exist in this tree, so the test pins the proposer and not the round. Size moved from 135 to 133 on 2026-09-28 with the upstream merge through a012e2bc, which removed two ctest registrations: ninfer_softmax_attention_nvfp4_test and ninfer_softmax_attention_k8v4_test, both SKIP_RETURN_CODE 77 wrappers around ninfer_softmax_attention_test with a --nvfp4-only or --k8v4-only flag. That is a consolidation and not a coverage loss: the test now takes --kv-dtype bf16|int8|fp8|nvfp4|k8v4|all and its default, no --kv-dtype, runs the whole storage matrix in one invocation, with kAttentionNvfp4Criterion and kAttentionK8V4Criterion still in causal_cache.cpp. The default run therefore covers every KV representation, where the two wrappers had to be listed and skipped individually. required_tests and optional_tests are unchanged, because the removed entries were never in either. Size moved from 133 to 135 on 2026-09-29 with the upstream merge through d44ab584, which added two registrations and removed none: ninfer_bench_fixtures_test, in tests/cmake/BenchSupportTests.cmake, and ninfer_qwen3_5_dflash_prefill_real_test, in tests/models/qwen3_5/tests.cmake. The count is derived by enumerating ninfer_add_test and ninfer_add_op_test across all thirteen registration sites under tests/ and differencing that set against HEAD, because deriving it from recorded numbers alone is what produced two wrong counts in this file before, and because a first pass that scanned two files and one registration macro found the net as zero and missed both. ninfer_qwen3_5_dflash_prefill_real_test joins required_tests rather than optional_tests: it reads NINFER_TEST_ARTIFACT and skips without it, and it passed against this product's artifact in 6.73 s, so the evidence this gate exists to demand is available here. optional_tests is unchanged, since ninfer_bench_fixtures_test needs no artifact and so belongs to neither list. known_failures is unchanged, with dflash_real and moe_real still failing by construction, so the run is 133/135 passing against a recorded two known failures. Size moved from 152 to 155 on 2026-10-06 by splitting ninfer_context_kv_materialize_test into four entries partitioned by batch: the sweep is host-oracle-bound and was the suite longest at 166.1 s, and the filter keeps the assertion rather than changing it -- each batch capacity check compares against the peak that batch own cases reached, a maximum over exactly the cases the filter keeps or drops, and the four entries were verified to report the same peaks as the unparameterised binary (41,943,040 / 655,360 / 983,040 / 1,310,720 / 1,638,400 / 1,966,080 / 1,863,680 / 1,966,080). The four cost 82 / 26 / 22 / 34 s, so the same work now runs concurrently instead of in one process. Size moved from 155 to 157 on 2026-10-07 with upstream dev through 81c8ce09 (tuple schemas, bounded numbers, choice and regex constrained decoding, and eight bf16 Op shapes): upstream added ninfer_regex_choice_test and ninfer_regex_choice_oracle_test. The eight Op commits changed no registration; the count is derived by enumerating ninfer_add_test and ninfer_add_op_test across tests/ and differencing that set against HEAD, which is what produced the wrong counts here twice before. Size moved from 157 to 156 on 2026-10-11 by deleting ninfer_ngram_selection_test together with the header it was the only user of: ngram_selection.h had no production caller once the copy-drafting core was replaced (59bcf3ef withdrew the CLI flags, the counters and prompt_lookup.h, and speculative_prepare_verify_inputs carries no copy override), and the test said so itself, calling itself a control rather than coverage. It pinned a decision nothing makes. Verified tree-wide before deleting: select_copy_round, CopyRoundDecision and selection_source_counts appear in that header and that test and nowhere else, and the registration is removed in the same change. Size moved from 193 to 195 on 2026-10-30 with the upstream/dev 458863be2 merge, which added ninfer_token_input_test (tests/text) and ninfer_qwen3_5_terminal_publication_real_test (a second scenario of the prefix runner, registered by add_test rather than ninfer_add_test). The count is from ctest -N on the merged tree (195), not from differencing recorded numbers. ninfer_moe_tp2_test is registered upstream too but only for NINFER_TARGET=dgx_spark, so it is not part of this tree's 195.
